A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeuralWalker work. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and sufficiently complete for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original NeuralWalker results on 19 benchmark datasets, component ablations, sampling sensitivity experiments, and sampling-variability measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds ZINC pretraining experiments and a CNN-without-message-passing comparison.

M1.justification: The core sampler, walk encoder, aggregation, and message-passing architecture remain unchanged. Section 5.2 adds an optional training extension: reconstruct masked positional encodings, optionally followed by masked-attribute pretraining.

E1.justification: The same 19 datasets and downstream tasks are retained. v2 adds masked positional-encoding and attribute-prediction training tasks on ZINC, extending training-task coverage without introducing another dataset or domain.

E2.justification: GRIT is added to all five Benchmarking GNNs comparisons and the two peptide comparisons in Tables 1–2. Table 4 adds a masked-attribute pretraining comparator, while Tables 6b and 13 add a CNN-without-message-passing configuration identified with CRaWL. Existing benchmark comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: ZINC training increases from 500 to 2000 epochs, MNIST/CIFAR10 model sizes change from 474K to 112K parameters, and PascalVOC-SP changes from five blocks of width 56 to six of width 52. v2 also introduces the ZINC pretraining experiment. These are documented protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new ZINC comparison tests no pretraining, masked attributes, masked positional encodings, and their sequential combination. A new CNN-without-message-passing control tests the contribution of message passing. Earlier component ablations and sampling analyses remain, including v1 Table 5's results relocated to v2 Table 13.

E5.justification: Both versions report four-run benchmark/ablation statistics, ten-run OGB/node-classification statistics, and local variability over five independently sampled walk sets. Although v2's main ablation summary omits standard deviations, they remain in Appendix Table 13. No changed uncertainty-estimation practice or increased run count is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces NeuralWalker's ZINC MAE 0.065 with 0.053 using pretraining, MNIST accuracy 98.760 with 98.692, and CIFAR10 accuracy 80.027 with 76.903. Changed training/model settings prevent treating these as controlled performance gains or losses. New GRIT entries overturn the previous first-place rankings on PATTERN and CLUSTER, and new pretraining/control results expand the evidence. v2 Table 14 nevertheless retains the earlier detailed scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds an earth-mover-distance stability bound, defines a bounded-size subgraph-isomorphism test and proves a related distinguishability result, and strengthens Theorem 4.4 accordingly. It also adds the Mamba-based complexity theorem and proof in Appendix C.3. These substantially extend the formal analysis beyond v1's stability, injectivity, and 1-WL results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution summary, and conclusion retain the central claims: combining random-walk sequences with message passing, supporting different sequence/GNN/GT architectures, and demonstrating improvements across 19 benchmarks including up to 13% on the highlighted LRGB datasets. The newly emphasized 1.6-million-node scalability was already reported in v1.

C2.justification: v2 develops the breadth-first local-subtree versus depth-first walk explanation, replacing Figure 1's centrality/cycle emphasis. It adds interpretations involving CNN universality, superiority over CRaWL, and stability relative to tree-mover distance, while removing v1's directed-graph interpretation of the CIFAR10 advantage. The explicit limitations concerning sampling coverage and available long-range benchmarks remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies 15% positional masking, replacement by 0.5 vectors, sequential pretraining stages, and use of ZINC without external data. Appendix hyperparameter and runtime entries are revised, including ZINC's total training time from 2.1 to 8.4 hours. Hardware, optimizer information, and code-access information remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds connections to BERT, GRIT, node2vec/DeepWalk, tree-mover distance, and universality literature, while removing several general application citations. Its comparison with CRaWL expands from convolutional receptive-field limitations to explicit universality and expressivity arguments. The principal related-work categories and closest prior methods remain the same.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, and experimental discussion undergo extensive rewriting. Former Sections 3.3–3.6 become subsections of Model Architecture, global-message-passing formulas move to Appendix B.2, and the theoretical appendix is reorganized. This is substantial editorial restructuring beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn around a star-subgraph example. v2 adds the pretraining table, splits the main ablation display into two panels, and relocates the full ablation table to the appendix. Other displays are resized or repositioned, but the architecture diagram, encoding illustration, and sampling plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: The pretraining controls, GRIT comparisons, and more explicit theoretical discussion provide useful additions. However, v2 introduces unresolved reporting conflicts: Table 1 gives CIFAR10 accuracy 76.903%, while Table 14 retains 80.03% without reconciling their settings; Table 6b's purported best CNN PascalVOC-SP score is 0.4652 despite 0.4790 in Table 13. These weaknesses obscure the revised empirical support, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
